You are advising on requirements for an existing, working, single-user music-video
production studio. Be concrete and skeptical. Do not pad.

THE STACK AS IT EXISTS (do not propose replacing it):
- Python 3.12, FastAPI + Jinja2 templates + htmx. Minimal JS, no build step, no
  React/Vue/Svelte. One SQLite database. Runs on a tailnet, single user, no auth.
- ffmpeg for ALL deterministic audio/video work (trim, crossfade, concat,
  beat-matched cuts, tempo ramp, branding overlays, fade-to-black).
- ComfyUI (3 GPU backends behind SwarmUI) for generation: Qwen-Image-Edit for
  reference stills, LTX-2.5 for 4.8s video clips, ACE-Step for music.
- A song -> storyboard -> reference frames -> clips -> assembled video pipeline
  already works end to end. Sets/playlists mix multiple songs with transitions.

WHAT WE ARE ABOUT TO SPECIFY. For each, tell me (a) the requirements we have
probably MISSED, (b) the specific failure modes that bite people who build this,
(c) what NOT to build:

1. A browser DAW-like timeline editor for sets. Waveform-as-card, scrubbing
   timeline with timestamps, playback, then volume/fade automation curves drawn
   per channel, left/right channel split, and video-effect lanes tied to the
   audio timeline. Three modes: easy / normal / advanced. It must round-trip to
   ffmpeg filter graphs, since ffmpeg is what actually renders.
2. Audio export in WAV, FLAC and Ogg Vorbis alongside the current MP3.
3. Automated QC of generated media: images, audio, video clips, full videos and
   sets. Detect artifacts, measure "reference compliance" (does the render match
   the character reference), report percent variation, and state clearly what it
   can and cannot fix automatically.
4. Publishing to YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, X, Bluesky, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Odysee
   and SoundCloud, with a hard policy gate so adult-tier material can never reach
   a destination that forbids it.
5. Version-controlled prompt management for a per-album "story arc" (think a
   musical or opera: setting and through-line) and per-song storyboards derived
   from it, with AI-assisted rewrite and full CRUD history.

THEN, THE PART I CARE MOST ABOUT:
Name SPECIFIC open-source projects we should read or borrow from, for any of the
five areas. Requirements for what you name:
- It must be real and you must be confident of the exact repo path.
- Prefer projects with commits in 2025 or 2026. Say so if you are unsure of
  recency; do NOT guess a star count or a date.
- Say in one line WHAT to take from it (an algorithm, a data model, a UI
  interaction, a filter-graph technique) rather than "look at this, it's similar".
- Web-audio waveform/timeline libraries, ffmpeg filter-graph builders, video QC
  and artifact-detection tools, and multi-platform upload libraries are all
  directly relevant.

If you are not sure a project exists or is maintained, SAY SO explicitly rather
than producing a plausible name. A fabricated repo costs me more than a missing
one. Mark anything uncertain with UNSURE.
